text.p: Italian debt markets continued to beat a sharp retreat in late trade, ending around 40 basis points down on the day in a generally weaker bond environment.
The March futures contract on LIFFE was 57 basis points down at 127.23. "We are targetting 126.90 on the downside tomorrow," one broker at an Italian bank in London said.
The July 2006 Btp closed 40 basis points down at 108.00 with the yield at 7.69 percent and the spread over the benchmark 10-year Bund 177 basis points.
Dealers noted the March contract made a firm start in which it had headed up to fill in a chart gap at 128.22 and 128.14.
But the market then quietened in the wait for U.S. inflation data, which came in line with expectations. However dealers said a later bout of selling triggered stop losses.
"Btps are a bit uncertain on the direction," one broker said. "The contract has been in a positive trend for many months and now that is coming under pressure."
"People are changing their views on Btps and wondering how long the contract can keep going on," he added.
Players watched progress amid EU finance ministers in Dublin before a full summit on Friday, with ministers meeting today on a budget accord to keep members' deficits under control.
The full summit of European leaders starts on Friday.
